The specifications you're referring to — **3B Parameters, Hidden Size: 4096, Layers: 16, Heads: 32, Sequence Length: 4096** — describe the architectural details of a **large language model (LLM)**.

While you mention "from a LLM released today," these specs match very closely with **Microsoft's **(phi-3-mini).

Even though the model might have been announced or released recently, it appears you're referencing **Phi-3-mini**, which is part of Microsoft's Phi-3 series of compact, efficient language models.

Here’s how the specs align:

| Parameter | Value | Explanation |
|---------|-------|-----------|
| **Parameters** | **3B** | The model has approximately **3 billion parameters**, making it a small-to-mid-sized LLM optimized for efficiency and on-device or edge deployment. |
| **Hidden Size** | **4096** | This is the dimensionality of the model’s hidden states (i.e., the size of the token embeddings and transformer hidden layers). A high hidden size relative to model size indicates a "wide and shallow" architecture. |
| **Layers** | **16** | Number of transformer layers (blocks). This is relatively shallow compared to larger models (e.g., Llama-3-70B has 80+ layers), supporting faster inference. |
| **Heads** | **32** | Number of attention heads in multi-head attention. With hidden size 4096, each head has 4096/32 = 128 dimensions. |
| **Sequence Length** | **4096** | Maximum context length the model can handle. Some variants in the Phi-3 family support up to 128K via extended context methods, but 4096 is standard for base configurations. |

🔍 **Why this architecture?**  
The Phi-3-mini uses a **"mixture-of-experts-inspired" training** with dense architecture, achieving strong performance for its size. It's designed for **on-device** or **low-latency applications**, balancing capability and efficiency.

🧠 Despite being only 3B parameters, it's reported to **perform competitively with models like Llama-3-8B and Mixtral 8x7B** on certain benchmarks, thanks to high-quality training data and modern architectural choices.

✅ So, to answer your question:
> These specs most likely belong to **Microsoft Phi-3-mini**, a state-of-the-art small language model released in **March 2024**, optimized for performance on mobile and edge devices.

Let me know if you have a specific model name or release date in mind — I can confirm if it's a new variant!
